title: A determination of whether the dimensionless constants of physics are calculable

concept.text: Strings 2000 problem 1 (proposed by David Gross): are all the measurable dimensionless parameters that characterize the physical universe calculable in principle, or are some merely determined by historical or quantum mechanical accident and uncalculable? Sources given: https://preskill.caltech.edu/millennium.html ; https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v54.i10.14_2.online.pdf ; https://x.com/martinmbauer/status/1779906631003697211.

change_log.change: Added by hand to PHY on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the ten Physics Problems for the Next Millennium chosen at the Strings 2000 conference (University of Michigan) by a panel of Michael Duff, David Gross and Edward Witten; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Calculability of the dimensionless constants of physics
page.definition: A determination of whether physical laws fix every measurable dimensionless constant—a number independent of measurement units, such as a mass ratio—or leave at least one dependent on historical conditions or a quantum outcome. Calculating a probability distribution must be distinguished from calculating the particular value observed.

goal.need: Tegmark and colleagues' 2006 inventory contained 26 dimensionless inputs for particle physics and 5 additional inputs for cosmology. Explaining these 31 inputs, or establishing why laws determine only probabilities for some of them, would distinguish consequences of physical laws from contingent properties of our universe.

figures.caption: Inputs in Tegmark and colleagues' 2006 inventory
figures.note: This is the paper's model-dependent inventory, not a fixed count for every possible theory. Dimensional quantities are expressed in Planck units.

statements.body: Strings 2000 selection panel: Michael Duff, David Gross and Edward Witten
statements.quote: Are all the (measurable) dimensionless parameters that characterize the physical universe calculable in principle
statements.context: This opens problem 1, proposed by David Gross and presented on 15 July 2000; the question also permits historical or quantum contingency.

statements.body: National Research Council, Committee on Elementary-Particle Physics
statements.quote: What determines this structure and the values of these parameters?
statements.context: The question concerns the Standard Model's particle masses, interactions and independent parameters, discussed in Chapter 3.

completion.title: An empirically supported theory establishes whether all dimensionless constants are fixed by physical laws.
completion.criterion: A peer-reviewed theoretical result, independently checked and supported by discriminating observations, establishes either that physical laws fix every measurable dimensionless parameter or that at least one retains historical or quantum contingency within the supported theory. The argument identifies any remaining initial conditions and vacuum choices. A numerical fit, an uncompleted calculation or the existence of several mathematical solutions does not establish contingency.
completion.set_by: Atlas; operational interpretation of Strings 2000 problem 1. The conference published the question without an adjudication procedure.
completion.basis: Searches of the Strings 2000 problem list, National Research Council discussions, fundamental-constants reviews and string-phenomenology reviews found the question and partial research criteria, but no published adjudication procedure. This test retains Gross's two possible answers. Its conclusion is conditional on the empirically supported theory; finite measurements cannot establish a statement about every conceivable theory.

milestones.title: A string vacuum reproduces the Standard Model gauge group and chiral matter spectrum.
milestones.criterion: A four-dimensional string construction contains the Standard Model's interaction symmetries and chiral spectrum—the net left- and right-handed fermion representations—with no additional chiral matter. Cvetič and colleagues reported a construction of order 10^15 F-theory compactifications with this spectrum and gauge coupling unification in 2019. These are theoretical constructions, not experimentally identified vacua.
milestones.set_by: String-phenomenology model-building convention, described by Marchesano, Shiu and Weigand in Section 2.2. This benchmark concerns the string-theory route only.
milestones.threshold_quote: contain the SM gauge group and chiral spectrum and are absent of chiral exotics

milestones.title: One string vacuum combines the Standard Model, stabilised moduli and observed cosmology.
milestones.criterion: A single string vacuum reproduces the Standard Model, including its vector-like matter and precise flavour structure, while stabilising all moduli—fields describing continuous choices such as the size and shape of extra dimensions—and incorporating cosmology consistent with observation. Stabilising a chosen vacuum does not establish why nature selects it. The 2024 review identifies the combined construction as a remaining challenge.
milestones.set_by: String-phenomenology research criterion stated by Marchesano, Shiu and Weigand in Section 6. This benchmark concerns string compactifications only; the source supplies no numerical cosmological tolerance.
milestones.threshold_quote: with all moduli stabilized and incorporating a realistic cosmology.

milestones.title: An ensemble theory computes the joint probability distribution of its dimensionless constants.
milestones.criterion: For a theory allowing different constants in different regions, calculate their joint distribution using both the physical prior and observation-selection effects. Specifying possible values alone is insufficient. Tegmark and colleagues supplied a conditional axion dark-matter example in 2006, rather than a prediction for the complete parameter vector.
milestones.set_by: Statistical-prediction criterion applied to ensemble cosmologies by Tegmark, Aguirre, Rees and Wilczek, Sections I.C and V. This is a criterion for ensemble theories, without a numerical acceptance cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: they are neither testable nor falsifiable unless their probabilistic predictions can be computed.

milestones.title: Independent measurements corroborate a theory's discriminating predictions for dimensionless constants.
milestones.criterion: Measurements not used to fit a candidate theory's predictions agree with its predicted constants or their joint distribution, including relevant selection effects. The observations distinguish that prediction from alternatives. No universal precision, significance or experimental sample-size threshold is specified.
milestones.set_by: Atlas; searches of the Strings 2000 problem statement, academy discussions and the cited prediction frameworks found no constants-specific experimental acceptance threshold. This operationalises their requirement to confront physical predictions with observation.

not_found: No published adjudication procedure was found for deciding Strings 2000 problem 1.
No framework-independent laboratory-to-completion milestone sequence was found; the published theoretical benchmarks concern particular research routes.
No universal experimental precision or significance threshold was found for corroborating an explanation of dimensionless constants.

results.finding: F-theory construction: approximately 10^15 compactifications with the exact Standard Model chiral spectrum.
results.detail: The models have the Standard Model gauge group and three chiral generations. The count is an estimate; additional vectorlike matter may be present. These are theoretical constructions.
results.quote:
We present Oð1015Þ string compactifications with the exact chiral spectrum of the standard model of
particle physics.

results.finding: One string compactification embeds a Standard Model-like quiver with 3 families and closed-string moduli stabilisation in a de Sitter minimum.
results.detail: The construction yields an MSSM low-energy spectrum, but the excerpt does not establish the precise observed flavour structure, stabilisation of all moduli, or a complete cosmology consistent with observation. Its cosmological viability is conditional.
results.quote:
The model features closed string moduli stabilisation with a de Sitter minimum
from T-branes, supersymmetry broken by the Kähler moduli, and the MSSM as the low
energy spectrum.

results.finding: Conditional axion model (sample size not applicable): selection-weighted distribution for 1 of 31 parameters peaks near the observed dark matter density.
results.detail: The result assumes Peccei–Quinn symmetry breaking before or during inflation. It combines an axion prior with astrophysical selection effects, but does not calculate the joint distribution of the complete parameter vector.
results.quote:
we ﬁnd that this probability distribution,
computed at stable solar systems, is arguably peaked near th e observed dark matter density.

results.finding: A multiverse model calculates observation-weighted probabilities for six macroscopic dimensionless constants; sample size not applicable.
results.detail: The calculation combines assumed physical priors with observer and habitability weights. It does not compute the complete joint distribution of all constants: additional parameters are absorbed into an unspecified factor, and the priors depend on theoretical assumptions.
results.quote: Our focus is on deriving probabilities for the six macroscopic dimensionless constants that most strongly dictate the structure of our universe.
